Another repro is to download `Godot_v4.4.1-stable_win32.exe` from the release page, dropping it where `project.godot` from the MRP is located and then running it. No export needed.

The problem is that that build doesn't have any symbols and if I build with `scons platform=windows target=editor arch=x86_32 d3d12=yes debug_symbols=yes` from the `4.4.1-stable` tag myself then it runs fine (and an export also works fine if I build `template_release` instead). I'm using Windows 11 and MSVC 2022 v17.13.6.

Maybe someone can tell me what the exact commandline is that is used to create the win32 build? (or if a build with symbols exists)

These are the options used for official builds: https://github.com/godotengine/godot-build-scripts/blob/main/build-windows/build.sh#L7-L8
The most relevant is `production=yes` which enables mainly `lto=full` (with GCC).
The toolchain used is MinGW with GCC 14.2.1 (on Fedora 41): https://github.com/godotengine/build-containers?tab=readme-ov-file#toolchains

It's not uncommon for bugs to be specific to the toolchain and/or LTO. For the record, LTO with MSVC doesn't work well with Godot and isn't really supported.

I managed to create a MinGW build but it crashes on startup (also without trying to run the repro). It's taking me too much time to get a callstack for this, so I'm going to give up. If someone else has things setup correctly for building x86_32 then I'd be willing to take a look at the callstack.

I'm not deeply familiar with that stuff, but it seems indeed that `-msse2` isn't sufficient, we also need to set `-mfpmath=sse` to opt into SSE floating point arithmetic instead of the default x87 (or `-mtune/-march=pentium4` or something, but I'm not clear on how clang deals with those so being explicit might be better).
